intro.title: Put AI to Work on Real Business Processes
paragraphs: Every business has work that is repetitive but too messy for simple rules: reading invoices and claim forms, answering the same customer questions, checking documents, writing routine content, testing software after every change. AI automation combines machine learning, natural language processing and process automation to handle this work quickly and consistently.

We build practical AI automation that plugs into your existing systems. Conversational AI answers customers on your website, chat and phone. Intelligent document processing reads invoices, claims and forms, extracts the data and sends it to your ERP or CRM. AI-powered testing finds bugs faster. Custom large language model (LLM) applications search your knowledge, draft responses and summarise information, with human review wherever accuracy matters.

We start with a short discovery to find the use cases with the clearest return, prove them with a pilot, then scale. Your data stays secure and private throughout. Pair AI with our <api>API integration</api> services, or <contact>tell us which process you want to automate</contact>.

comparison.title: Rule-Based Automation or AI-Powered Intelligent Automation?
comparison.subtitle: Traditional automation follows fixed rules. AI automation can read, understand and decide. Here is the difference.

columns.title: Rule-based automation (RPA)

cons: Breaks when formats or screens change
Cannot read unstructured documents or emails
No understanding of language or intent

columns.title: AI-powered intelligent automation
columns.bestFor: Best for: documents, conversations and judgement calls
pros: Combines with RPA for end-to-end automation
cons: Needs good data and careful testing

faqs.title: AI Automation FAQs
faqs.subtitle: Quick answers about using AI to automate work.

items.a: AI automation uses artificial intelligence, such as natural language processing, machine learning and computer vision, to perform tasks that normally need human judgement, like reading documents, answering customer questions or classifying requests, and then triggers actions in your systems.

items.q: What is the difference between AI automation and RPA?
items.a: RPA follows fixed rules on structured data and screens. AI automation can understand unstructured content like emails, documents and speech and handle variations. Many solutions combine both: AI to understand, RPA or APIs to act.

items.q: How can AI chatbots improve customer service?
items.a: AI chatbots answer common questions instantly, 24/7, using your own knowledge base, collect details, update orders or bookings and hand complex cases to human agents with full context, reducing wait times and support costs.

items.q: Can AI accurately process invoices and documents?
items.a: Yes. Intelligent document processing combines OCR and machine learning to extract data from invoices, claims and forms with high accuracy, and sends low-confidence items to a person for review, so errors do not slip through.

items.q: How is AI used in software testing?
items.a: AI helps generate test cases from requirements, keep automated tests working when the interface changes, detect visual differences and prioritise risky areas, making test automation faster and more reliable.

items.q: Is our data safe when using AI?
items.a: Yes. We use private, enterprise-grade AI deployments, encryption, access control and data minimisation, and can keep sensitive data entirely in-house when required.

items.q: How much does AI automation cost?
items.a: An AI pilot typically costs $5,000 to $15,000, a production AI automation solution $15,000 to $50,000, and enterprise AI programmes $50,000 or more, depending on use case and integrations.
